outcome: No progress found on the infinitude question itself since 26 January 2024: no Fibonacci-Wieferich prime, Pell-Wieferich prime, or Lucas-Wieferich prime for a general pair (a,-1) has been found by any search, and no unconditional or conditional theoretical result establishing infinitude of these primes (as opposed to infinitude of their complement, the non-Wieferich primes) has appeared in the window.
summary: The bullet asks whether, for a fixed integer a>0, there are infinitely many Lucas-Wieferich primes for the pair (a,-1) — i.e. primes p for which the Wieferich-type congruence *holds* (U_{p-e} ≡ 0 mod p²) for the Lucas sequence with parameters (a,-1); the a=1 case is Fibonacci-Wieferich primes and a=2 is Pell-Wieferich primes. I confirmed the triage's finding and extended its search. No new Fibonacci-Wieferich or Pell-Wieferich prime has been found since the frozen revision (the known bounds remain the pre-2024 PrimeGrid limits, roughly 9.7×10^14–1.9×10^17 for Fibonacci and below 10^9 for Pell, per the current Wieferich prime Wikipedia article, which itself contains no post-2022 developments on these variants). On the theoretical side, the active research program in this exact area (2021 Fang–Ren/Ribenboim-style paper on Lucas non-Wieferich primes in arithmetic progressions; a March 2025 paper 'The abc conjecture implies infinitely many non-Wieferich places for fixed bases in number fields' (arXiv:2503.19144); an August 2025 paper on Wieferich primes in number fields and the Ankeny-Artin-Chowla/Mordell conjectures (arXiv:2508.08472); and a December 2025 paper on p-adic valuations of Möbius duals of Lucas sequences and Wall-Sun-Sun primes (arXiv:2512.03481)) all address either (a) the complement question — infinitely many non-Wieferich (or non-Lucas-Wieferich) primes, which is the opposite congruence condition and does not bear on this bullet — or (b) number-field analogues/generalizations that are variants under §3.1, not cases of the rational-integer pair (a,-1) question as stated. None of these establishes, conditionally or otherwise, that there are infinitely many primes p with U_{p-e}(a,-1) ≡ 0 (mod p²) for any fixed a. No AI system appears anywhere in this literature or in the computational searches (which use classical sieve/modular-exponentiation methods, e.g. PrimeGrid's distributed computing project, not any AI/ML technique). I am satisfied nothing has happened to the stated question in the window.
competing_reading: One could argue the 2512.03481 Möbius-dual paper's discussion of Wall-Sun-Sun primes is adjacent enough to count as 'progress' on the broader family of Wieferich-type conjectures, and one could argue the number-field papers (2503.19144, 2508.08472) are generalizations that 'contain' the rational case as a special instance. But in each case the actual theorem proved is about a different congruence (non-Wieferich, i.e. the failure of the congruence) or a different domain (number fields, Wall-Sun-Sun primes for Fibonacci divisibility by p rather than p²-Wieferich-type congruences for Lucas sequences), so under the case-vs-variant test in §3.1 none of them changes what a careful person would write in this bullet's entry.
what_would_settle_it: A paper or search result that either exhibits a Fibonacci-Wieferich, Pell-Wieferich, or general Lucas-Wieferich(a,-1) prime, or that proves (conditionally or unconditionally) infinitude of primes satisfying U_{p-e}(a,-1) ≡ 0 (mod p²) for some or all a, dated after 26 January 2024.
